When somebody says, "I am God, so I can kill," take it as a sign they could really hurt someone. To lead them back to not hurting anyone, start from what they believe, like the lines below do by saying God is in everyone. Arguing ("No you're not," "That's delusional") can make them dig in to prove they're God. And if you nod along as if hurting someone could be spiritually fine, they might think you're okay with them doing it.

Ask before you touch someone who's tripping, even to put your hand on their heart: "Would touch help, or would you rather have space?" Even a hug can be too much when they're already overwhelmed. And if you hold them down, they might feel attacked and fight you. If they'd rather have space, sit about six feet away and only talk if they want to.

Stop as soon as they say stop. Pulling away or freezing means stop too, since they might be too overwhelmed to tell you to stop. Ask again whenever you can't tell what they want. Be honest with yourself about why you want to touch them, and hold off if it's mostly to calm yourself down. Never touch them in a sexual way, even if they ask you to.

It might look passive, but this is how you become unhookable. When you meet a demon with love, the demon has nothing to hook into, since its hooks only catch on hatred and fear.

If someone's too overwhelmed to send love, because they're sick or too scared to think straight, help them get steady first. Turn the lights down, and get them a doctor if they need one. Leave the demon talk until they can think straight again.
